x: Alby Bird was our last man, and he could not be expected to give Halford (L.A.C.) and Barnes (Achilles) a start. Bird held his position, however, and was content to ease off in the finishing straight when third place was secure (South London H. were fourth) and first and second teams could not be overtaken.

Pack in place of Barnes would, in our humble opinion, have represented a few yards improvement. However, we are not in the favoured position of the Selectors, and we can only hope that next season our man will secure his full share of honours.

John Knifton was 24th in Section A Barnes, Belderson, Beecham and Keown, 6th 7th 30th and 32nd respectively in Section B; Eglington, Cameron, McLennan, Duncan,Wilson and Doubleday between 18 and 62 in Section C; Bushman, East and Logan 14th,15th and 34th in Section D.

If Thomas maintains his form, Middleton gets really fit, Ray Hall gets going over the slightly longer distances, and our youngsters Barnes, Knifton, King etc. continue to improve then we shall be taking the gold instead of the silver and bronze.

Even the loss of King, Barnes and Cameron during the race did not affect the result. In the individual race Ray Middleton walked exceptionally well and coming thro' in his usual style was only 43 seconds short of catching the winner, Nihill.
